message.content:
**Famous 19th‑Century Dancers**

| Name | Nationality | Dance Form | Notable Contributions |
|------|-------------|------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swiss/Italian | Romantic ballet | Pioneered the ethereal “flying” style; first to dance en pointe with a light, airy technique. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Classical ballet | Known for her virtuoso technique and dramatic stage presence; popularized the “Elssler” style of expressive footwork. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1888) | Italian | Classical ballet | Renowned teacher and choreographer; authored *L’Art de la Danse* (1842), a foundational text on ballet technique. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Classical ballet | Master choreographer of the Imperial Russian Ballet; created iconic ballets such as *The Sleeping Beauty* and *Swan Lake* (though premiered in 1877). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1799–1868) | French | Classical ballet | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841); known for his elegant, narrative choreography. |
| **Martha Graham** (1894–1991) | American | Modern dance | Though her career peaked in the 20th century, she was born in the late 19th century and later revolutionized modern dance. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Classical ballet | Famous for her lyrical style and the worldwide success of *The Dying Swan* (1905). |
| **John L. T. (John) T. (John) T.** |  |  |  |
